subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that active skill's host-run exec path, and what isolation rule prevents unrelated exec leakage?
rationale: Source and release evidence show the reported auth path is still blocked, but the repair intentionally moves secrets into executable child environments and overlaps an open inverse secret-leak issue.

options.title: Allow Active-Skill Configured Keys
options.body: Permit only env keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name filter, keep dangerous host/runtime names blocked, and test both intended delivery and unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Require Metadata Declarations
options.body: Keep the current metadata-only sensitive allowlist and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary credential-shaped keys in `skills.entries.*.env` are not promised.

options.title: Defer To New Credential Contract
options.body: Leave the current sanitizer unchanged until a SecretRef, plugin-owned, or per-call trusted sandbox env design is approved.

recommendation.title: Allow Active-Skill Configured Keys
recommendation.body: Permit only env keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name filter, keep dangerous host/runtime names blocked, and test both intended delivery and unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a credential-to-exec security boundary, and recent history ties this handle to SecretRef and host exec env hardening.
